title: Application cannot import or start without a running PostgreSQL server
reproduction_prerequisites: Python 3.11 with psycopg2-binary installed; no PostgreSQL server running on localhost:5432; network limited to PyPI/npm/GitHub so PostgreSQL cannot be installed via apt
exact_reproduction_steps: 1. Create a venv and install flask+psycopg2-binary from PyPI. 2. From the repo root run: python -c "from apps.web.app import app". 3. Observe the traceback. Alternatively run python verify_readiness.py and observe the database connectivity check fails.
expected_behavior: The Flask application object should construct and the readiness check should report database connectivity or a clear
evidence_source: Import of apps.web.app raises psycopg2.OperationalError: connection to server at "localhost" port 5432 failed: Connection refused. The failure originates in Api/utils/utils.py -> DatabaseHub() -> database.Database._initialize_pool() -> ThreadedConnectionPool
relevant_file_endpoint_database_object: and is compounded by core/security/bootstrap_admin.py ensure_initial_admin() querying the users table at startup. No graceful degradation or offline mode exists.
browser_terminal_evidence: Terminal traceback captured during import attempt (2026-10-23 07:43) and during pytest unit runs ("connection to server at localhost:5432 failed: Connection refused"). verify_readiness.py database checks cannot execute.
column18: The operator cannot launch the UI or API at all without first provisioning and migrating a PostgreSQL database. The system is non-functional out of the box in any environment lacking PostgreSQL.
column19: Provision PostgreSQL as a documented hard prerequisite; ideally add lazy/failing-soft database initialization so the app can at least construct and show a clear setup/maintenance page when the database is unavailable. Guard bootstrap_admin and DatabaseHub so a missing database does not abort import.
